lines: Antonio Stradivari was a famous instrument maker.
He lived and worked in Italy in the 17th and 18th centuries.
His violins are considered to be the best around the world.
Scientists are unable to figure out what exactly makes his violins so incredible.
But a possible explanation is the strength of the wood used to make them.
From the 1700s to 1800s, the Earth went through a little ice age.
As a result of this cooling, the types of trees that Stradivari used for his violins were particularly hard and dense because of slow growth.
Hard wood is especially good for making violins.
Perhaps, if you were a violin maker and born in the 1700s, the world-best violins could be yours, not Stradivari’s.
